Header: Ceratitis cosyra, Ceratitis rosa, Bactrocera invadens

Prevention: Avoid planting citrus near alternative host plants (eg, guava, sheanut, mango etc.) or subject them to the same treatments
Collect dropped fruits regularly and bury least 50 cm below the soil surface outside of the field.
Alternatively put fruits in a thick black plastic bag, seal and expose to sunshine for 7 days
Harvest early (at physiological maturity) to prevent flies attacking fruits
Move harvested fruits out of field as early as possible as fruit flies will attack fruits even after harvest
Keep weeds reasonably low by slashing and weeding around the basins just before flowering
Conserve natural enemies such as ants, rove beetles, birds and parasitic wasps by avoiding use of pesticides
Monitoring: Start monitoring as soon as fruits begin to mature, search twice a week on fruits for adult fruit flies
Check fruits for signs of insect.
Look for small punctures or 'sting' marks on the skin where the fly lays its eggs, these are very small but some sticky gum may be present.
On mature citrus the sting mark might be a brown depressed spot and on immature citrus the green skin may colour prematurely round the sting
Cut open dropped fruits and check for the presence of maggots in them
For early detection and monitoring use: i) food baits e.g. waste brewers’ yeast 45ml/L of water or ripe fruits ii) pheromone traps with trimedlure, cuelure, or methyl eugenol (2 traps/ 50m 2 )
Take action as soon as fruit fly damage is observed or when flies are detected in the traps
Direct Control: Regularly collect drop/fallen fruits and dispose off properly.
Dig and bury collected fruits to about 50 cm deep (length of one cutlass)
Collect fruits into thick, black plastic bags, tie bag firmly and expose to the sun for 7-10 days (duration may be longer during the rainy season).
Till the orchard top soil (5-10cm) to expose pupae to the sun, birds, poultry and parasites
Use lure and kill pheromone traps containing a mixture of 10ml methyl eugenol + 1ml insectide (see yellow list).
Set 4-6 traps per acre evenly spaced.
Set the traps at flowering and refill after every 8 weeks if locally made and 4 weeks if a commercial trap
Restrictions: When using a pesticide or botanical, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label
Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance
Always consult the most recent list of registered pesticides of
Appat (0.24 g/l)) at a ratio of 1 part product to 3 parts water.
Spray trees fully and repeat after 1 week.
Monitor for fruit flies before further applications.
Spinosad is highly toxic to aquatic invertebrates, do not use near waterways
Insecticides used as killing agents in pheromone traps:

Malathion, Organophosphate, IRAC 1B; Deltamethrin, pyrethroid with contact and residual activity, IRAC 3A; Acetamiprid, systemic neonicotinoid, IRAC 4A; lambda- cyhalothrin, pyrethroid contact and ingested, IRAC 3A
